availability.note: Free for study; no commercial use; uploaded audio may be reused for research.

provider.notes: AI for Thai (Partii) speech-to-text. Registry id and aliases: gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1809-1810; the standardized factory that live sessions use accepts nectec, aiforthai, ai4thai, partii, partii5 and partii4 (gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:444-446). The provider aliases partii4 and partii5 select the provider, not the engine. The vendor has no model parameter; partii4 and partii5 are gateway-defined ids mapped to URL paths, and the client's other spellings of them (config.rs:108-117) are model_aliases on their rows. default_model is partii4, which is NOT what the code does today. Today an empty or unknown model becomes partii5 (gateway/src/core/stt/nectec/config.rs:84-85, :234-238), whose vendor endpoint returns 404, so a default-configured session cannot transcribe. The fact-check requires that partii5 stop being the default, and partii4 is the only engine whose endpoint answers, so the map resolves an empty model to it and the client default must be changed in the same step: until it is, a push-to-talk session that names no model resolves to the partii4 row and keeps today's client, which dials partii5 and fails. The gateway's only client is an HTTP client that uploads after every 30 s of received audio, at hang-up or at a client commit (client.rs:510-545); it is not a transport. The vendor's public catalogue lists Partii as inactive. Thai only.

transports.disabled_reason: No file-upload adapter for live calls exists (not implemented). The only NECTEC client uploads after 30 s of received audio, cut at an arbitrary byte, or at hang-up. Before enabling, a check with a real key must show that the endpoint transcribes and what a success reply looks like; no success response has ever been observed.

measurements.conditions: A 1 s upload rejected for want of a valid key (quota error, no transcription): TLS setup, upload and a quota check, 616 ms of it upstream.

latency.notes: No latency is published for the API. NECTEC's 2022 product page (https://www.nectec.or.th/en/research/ainrg/stu.html) states 'Real-time-factor: 1.5x' for Partii 4.0 without saying whether that is faster or slower than real time. The only timed request was rejected before transcription.

gateway_client.notes: The request code to lift out is NectecStt::process_partii4, a private method that builds, sends and parses in one step: POST https://api.aiforthai.in.th/partii-webapi, header Apikey, multipart fields wavfile, outputlevel and outputformat. It has never produced a transcript against the vendor, and the repository's mock test covers the other engine (gateway/tests/mock_endpoint_e2e.rs:1537-1568 uses partii5 and the gateway's own assumed reply). Defects to fix when extracting: the reply type declares status as an integer (config.rs:353-354) while the live service sends the string 'False' on errors, so a success carrying a string status would fail to parse and lose every transcript (inferred; no success body has been seen); a missing or invalid key is answered with HTTP 429 and a monthly-quota message, which the client reports as rate limiting (client.rs:277) and the circuit breaker counts as an ordinary failure; the vendor echoes the API key inside the error body, which the client logs and returns to the caller (client.rs:267-283), and the same body would be sent to a valid key that has used up its monthly allowance, so a real key can reach the logs and the WebSocket client (inferred by the fact-check); confidence is a constant 0.9 (client.rs:377); the error callback is never invoked; the request timeout is 60 s (config.rs:49). Do not retry a 429 within a turn. The audio must be 16 kHz mono PCM16 WAV; the client's own validation rejects other session rates only on one construction path (config.rs:283-309).

segment_profile.rationale: One upload in flight instead of two (inferred): a free shared service with per-user limits per minute, day and month and a system-wide per-second cap, where throttling and a bad key both come back as HTTP 429, so bursts should be avoided. The 15 s timeout is a placeholder: nothing is published and the vendor's 'real-time factor 1.5x' may mean slower than real time, in which case the timeout must grow with segment length. The maximum segment stays at 25 s, but unlike Whisper's soft window the vendor's stated 30 s and 1 MB are hard limits on the whole padded upload (25 s plus padding is 25.9 s and about 829 kB), and the segment must be resampled to 16 kHz mono because no other format is accepted.

when_unusable.code_ref: gateway/src/core/stt/nectec/client.rs:510-545 (send_audio only buffers; an upload happens after 30 s of received audio, at hang-up or at a client commit)

refusal.text: NECTEC Partii transcribes uploaded files only; the vendor offers no streaming interface for this use. This gateway does not yet split a live call into utterances for it, so for a voice agent that decides when the caller has finished speaking no transcript would arrive in time to answer. Use a streaming transcription model, set the agent's turn detection to manual, or ask the operator to enable segmented speech-to-text for this deployment.

billing.notes: Free service with quotas that count calls per user per minute, per day and per month, plus a system-wide per-second cap; the numbers are shown only after login and may change without notice. Commercial use is prohibited; commercial terms are by contact with the vendor. No entry for this provider exists in gateway/src/config/pricing.rs (checked 2026-10-03), so no pricing_key is given.

provenance.notes: 'partii4' is a gateway-defined id (an SDK module name the gateway adopted). The vendor API has no model parameter; the engine is chosen by URL path, and this id selects /partii-webapi (config.rs:92-97). The vendor documents no streaming interface for third parties, and the file interface answers in the same request, so segmentation is the only way to use it on a call. The route answered on 2026-10-03, but only with a quota error. Thai only; no language hint, no prompt and no confidence are known. A live web demo over Socket.IO and a licensed gRPC product exist, but neither is an offered interface and the terms forbid scripted access to them. Vendor terms make this provider evaluation-only (provider availability): besides the provider note, the service may stop without notice and scripted access outside the provided channels is forbidden. This is the engine the map resolves an empty model to (provider default_model); the client itself still defaults to partii5.

provenance.notes: The vendor endpoint for this engine (POST https://api.aiforthai.in.th/partii5-poc) returned HTTP 404 from the vendor's origin server on 2026-10-03, with no key and with a bogus key, to both the audit and the fact-check. The vendor's gateway forwards the route without checking the key, so a valid key is expected to get the same 404 (inferred; not tried with a real key). 'partii5' is a gateway-defined id that selects the URL path /partii5-poc (config.rs:43, :92-97). The vendor's SDK 1.3.2 still posts there. The circuit breaker ignores HTTP 404 (gateway/src/core/stt/http_resilience.rs:132-135) and the hang-up upload error is discarded (client.rs:486), so today the failure is silent. The fact-check requires that this stop being the gateway default. provider.default_model in this file is already partii4; the client constant (config.rs:84-85) and its handling of unknown strings (config.rs:234-238) must be changed to match. Vendor terms make this provider evaluation-only (provider availability): besides the provider note, the service may stop without notice and scripted access outside the provided channels is forbidden.
